html:
A Catholic basilica in Yamoussoukro, built from 1985 to 1989 by order of Houphouet-Boigny and consecrated by Pope John Paul II in 1990.

Its dome is modelled on that of St Peter's Basilica in Rome, and it is one of the largest churches in the world. Houphouet said he paid for it himself; critics pointed to its cost while the country, hit by the fall in cocoa prices, cut spending. It stands in his home village, which he made the official capital in 1983. Ivory Coast is divided between Muslims, mostly in the north, and Christians, mostly in the south, and the building became a symbol of the elite of his era. See also the Catholic Church.
sum: A Catholic basilica in Yamoussoukro, built from 1985 to 1989 by order of Houphouet-Boigny and consecrated by Pope John Paul II in 1990.
